transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Matt Chen (Redwood AE), Aisha Patel (Redwood SE), Ravi Nair (Redwood Solutions Eng); Liam Roberts (Head of ML, NewWave), Sofia Alvarez (Infra Lead), Daniel Park (CTO), Maya Singh (PM)

[00:00:02] Matt Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a sec, appreciate you taking the time. i'm matt from redwood, with aisha and ravi.
[00:00:10] Liam Roberts: thanks matt. quick note we're on pacific, so 3pm here. we've got about an hour.
[00:00:16] Aisha Patel: great, i'll do a quick intro then dig into dedicated questions — feel free to interrupt. so high level, newwave told us they're evaluating dedicated capacity for production inference, want isolation and predictable throughput, is that right liam?
[00:00:29] Liam Roberts: yeah exactly, we're moving several models into prod next quarter. latency needs to be 50-200ms p95 on short prompts, and we expect bursts during end-of-month analytics runs.
[00:00:40] Sofia Alvarez: also want network isolation and customer-managed keys — we can't send raw logs off our vpc.
[00:00:46] Aisha Patel: understood. we typically recommend Redwood Dedicated for that — reserved GPU pools with VPC peering or private connection, KMS support, and optional on-prem package if you go that route later.
[00:00:57] Daniel Park: when you say reserved pools what's the SLA? and how do bursts work — we don't want to overcommit and pay for idle infra.
[00:01:06] Ravi Nair: good question. Dedicated has committed capacity lines that you reserve — you get predictable throughput and SLOs. for bursts we do a configurable burst policy: short-term burst capacity from a shared pool (if enabled) or auto-scaling within the dedicated fleet if you've allowed headroom. bursts are metered differently from committed usage.
[00:01:26] Maya Singh: can you share an example of cost math? like if we reserve 8 A100s vs host plus bursts?
[00:01:33] Matt Chen: yes we'll share a pricing sheet after, but rough rule of thumb — reserved is higher fixed cost but lower unit token cost and guaranteed latency. hosted pay-as-you-go avoids commit but you can see higher tail latency and possible throttling at peak, especially for large sequence workloads.
[00:01:50] Liam Roberts: our workloads are a mix — short Q&A prompts and longer batch summarization overnight. the summarization can be very long sequences.
[00:01:58] Aisha Patel: okay that matters for kernel selection and KV cache. for long sequence batch work you might want to use quantized variants and dedicate a different model variant in the dedicated pool to optimize memory. we can pin model versions per-pool.
[00:02:11] Sofia Alvarez: we care about encryption at rest and audit trails. how's the KMS integration? can we bring our own?
[00:02:18] Aisha Patel: yes, BYOK with customer KMS/HSM is supported for Private and Dedicated (depending on deployment). logs and audit trails can be shipped to your log collector — we support structured audit logs and AWS KMS/GCP KMS integrations. note: on hosted public API, BYOK is not available.
[00:02:33] Daniel Park: what about data residency? some customers require EU-only.
[00:02:37] Matt Chen: we have region pinning for Dedicated and Private. we can host your dedicated pool in a specific region and prevent fallback.
[00:02:44] Liam Roberts: latency targets — do you have GPU-level latency numbers? like p95 tokens per second on A100s or H100s?
[00:02:51] Ravi Nair: we publish performance profiles for verified models. rough numbers: for common open decoder models, with optimized kernels p95 single-request small prompt latency is under 100ms on H100 for 4k context; that varies with model size and seq length. we'll share detailed perf.
[00:03:05] Maya Singh: we run transformer LLMs with a lot of kv-cache reuse, is continuous batching going to break our tail latency?
[00:03:12] Aisha Patel: continuous batching is workload-aware — it tries to maximize throughput without violating configured latency SLOs. you can set strict latency SLOs to reduce batching and pay more per token, or loosen them to get better throughput.
[00:03:24] Liam Roberts: okay when you say "pin model versions" how do rollouts/rollbacks work?
[00:03:28] Ravi Nair: rollouts are config-level — you can do canary and A/B. Dedicated supports per-pool model version pinning and automatic fallback to a compatible variant on failure.
[00:03:38] Sofia Alvarez: security question: SOC2 and ISO — are you SOC2 Type II? and what level of pen-testing?
[00:03:44] Matt Chen: yes, Redwood is SOC2 Type II and we have ISO documentation; we'll attach the security pack. we do regular pen tests and provide reports under NDA.
[00:03:54] Daniel Park: what about network topology — do we get private link or VPC peering?
[00:03:58] Aisha Patel: both options — VPC peering or private connect depending on cloud. for on-prem we can do a private control plane and customer-managed networking.
[00:04:06] Liam Roberts: do you support SSO and RBAC for team-level access?
[00:04:09] Matt Chen: yes SSO (SAML/OIDC) and granular RBAC, audit logs per-token, and role mappings.
[00:04:16] Maya Singh: curious about cold starts — if we scale from zero to 20 GPUs during a big run, how long is the spin-up?
[00:04:23] Ravi Nair: spin-up depends on provider and instance types — cold start for bare machines might be few minutes. for Dedicated we recommend maintaining a small baseline capacity or using burst from our shared pool to avoid long cold starts. also warmup caches helps.
[00:04:36] Sofia Alvarez: can Redwood Dedicated co-exist with our on-prem later? we may want a hybrid.
[00:04:40] Aisha Patel: absolutely — hybrid is a common pattern. you can start on Dedicated in the cloud and later add Private/on-prem nodes, with the same control plane and rollout policies.
[00:04:50] Liam Roberts: for the POC we want to run our prompt set and a synthetic end-of-month burst to see tail behavior. what's your recommended size?
[00:04:58] Ravi Nair: for a POC, we usually provision a small dedicated pool that matches your baseline concurrency and a short burst window that simulates peak. suggest 4-8 GPUs for initial run depending on model size. we'll provide a benchmark template.
[00:05:11] Maya Singh: can you talk about caching patterns — prefix cache and KV caching, and how that affects cost?
[00:05:16] Aisha Patel: prefix caching can save a lot if you have repeated prompts; KV cache reuse is automatic across requests on the same session if routed to the same pool and the same model. caching reduces token compute cost but requires affinity/routing which Dedicated supports strongly.
[00:05:30] Liam Roberts: any gotchas around quantization — we saw some quality regressions in other infra when moving to 4-bit.
[00:05:36] Ravi Nair: yes quality can change. Redwood Optimize runs evals and recommends quantization profiles per-model and per-workload; you can run evals during the POC to validate.
[00:05:46] Sofia Alvarez: regarding compliance, we need an audit trail for who accessed model outputs for 12 months. can you retain logs that long?
[00:05:54] Matt Chen: yes for Dedicated/Private we can retain logs per-route for configurable retention, and offer long-term storage as an add-on.
[00:06:02] Liam Roberts: what's the support SLA for Dedicated?
[00:06:05] Matt Chen: dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and a support tier — enterprise support with 24/7 on-call is available for Dedicated customers.
[00:06:12] Maya Singh: do you have any references in fintech? we've got regulatory constraints.
[00:06:16] Matt Chen: we have customers in regulated sectors; we can provide redacted case studies and introduce you to references under NDA.
[00:06:23] Daniel Park: how does billing for bursts show up in invoices? we need predictable accounting lines.
[00:06:29] Ravi Nair: bursts are billed separately — you'll see committed charges and burst/overage line items. we provide per-token and per-GPU-hour breakdowns in the console.
[00:06:37] Liam Roberts: are there limits on model size for Dedicated? we push large 70B models and some custom weights.
[00:06:44] Aisha Patel: we support a wide range; for very large models we recommend multi-GPU sharding and we can advise on optimal placement. bring your model and we'll run an onboarding perf test.
[00:06:55] Sofia Alvarez: network egress — we need to ensure no consumer data leaves region, how do you enforce that?
[00:07:01] Matt Chen: region pinning plus disabling cross-region fallback will enforce residency; for strict needs, Private on-prem package avoids egress entirely.
[00:07:10] Maya Singh: what's the onboarding timeline?
[00:07:12] Matt Chen: typical Dedicated onboarding is 2-6 weeks depending on paperwork and provisioning. POC can be done faster if you share infra details.
[00:07:20] Liam Roberts: ok good. next steps?
[00:07:22] Matt Chen: recap: we'll send pricing, security pack, and a POC runbook. aisha will prepare the benchmark template. you (sofia) to share infra diagrams and traffic patterns.
[00:07:33] Liam Roberts: yes we'll aim to get infra diagrams over by end of week.
[00:07:37] Maya Singh: also please include an example burst policy and how it behaves during sustained peaks.
[00:07:42] Aisha Patel: noted, we'll include burst policy examples and a sample SLA.
[00:07:46] Daniel Park: can you also include the perf numbers for H100 vs A100?
[00:07:50] Ravi Nair: yes we'll attach model perf docs.
[00:07:54] Matt Chen: cool — any other blockers?
[00:07:57] Liam Roberts: nothing else from me. thanks all.
[00:08:01] Matt Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the deck and action items.

[00:40:00] (rest of call — aisha walked through deployment diagrams, there was a short screen share where the POC template was sketched, some cross talk on timing)

[00:56:00] Sofia Alvarez: quick clarification, you mentioned shared burst pool — is that multitenant? we prefer not to have noisy neighbor risks.
[00:56:07] Aisha Patel: it's isolated in policy — the shared pool is capacity the platform can allocate but we throttle per-tenant. for strict isolation we can disable shared burst and only use autoscale within your reserved fleet.
[00:56:20] Liam Roberts: perfect.
[00:56:22] Matt Chen: final next steps again: pricing + security pack (matt), POC runbook + benchmark (aisha), infra diagrams (sofia), schedule POC kickoff (ravi/matt) — aim for week of Apr 6.
[00:56:38] Meeting end: ~58 minutes

Notes on transcript quality: some words (kernel vs colonel) mistranscribed, proper nouns sometimes inconsistent.
